I feel like a video like this, if it claims to be explaining the psychology behind something game related, has to be spot on with the explanation or the entire thing is a waste. It might have been a mistake to try to describe the psycho-pharmacological manifestation of an acute stress response based on superficial research. Game produces jump-scare (acute stress), adrenaline is released causing all kinds of metabolic changes to support a survival response, when the adrenaline production is halted and the active adrenaline levels decreased, stored dopamine is released producing a euphoric/pleasure response. That's the basic loop which is nothing really new to a lot of people, so if we're going to elaborate on it we have to be a little careful in what we say and why.

The commentary on the behavior of crack and how it produces its high is where I had to stop. Crack doesn't trigger a massive release of dopamine. It functions as a dopamine re-uptake inhibitor, meaning it prevents the already present dopamine in the brain from being re-absorbed the way it normally would be, causing a dopamine backlog that simulates a massive dose. We don't need to be inadvertently creating parallels between video games and narcotics.
